transcript_tail.text: Good pivot — let me answer both directly. First, "are all users corrected?": no, I only fixed account 7's user (`user1`). Let me find **every** account-owner in the same broken state (owns an account but has no role on that account's fund), so we know the real blast radius and whether a backfill migration is warranted.

Here's the blast radius: **14 accounts across 11 more users** are in the exact same broken state as account 7 — all `userN@dev.familyfund.local` owners on fund 2, none with a role. So **no, only 1 of 12 affected users is corrected.**

A backfill is the right call. Before I write it, let me read the roles seeder to pick the correct vehicle (migration vs seeder) and reuse its role-creation logic safely — especially the permission dependency.

Now I have what I need. The `beneficiary` role grants `accounts.view-own`, `transactions.view-own`, `funds.view`, `reports.view`, `credit-lines.view-own` — and crucially `createFundRole()` calls `syncPermissions()`, which requires those permissions to already exist. So a backfill migration must ensure permissions exist first.

Let me check the latest migration filename so I can place a new one after it.
I'll write the prod-safe, idempotent backfill migration.

The backfill migration is written (idempotent, prod-safe: only adds the role, never downgrades admins, self-seeds the needed permissions). Now — **important**: applying it on the *current* code would spread the exact dashboard over-exposure and funds leak you just saw to all 11 users. So the backfill is coupled to the dashboard/scoping fixes; they should ship together.

Before I lay out the plan, let me ground the "what should a beneficiary actually see" question in the existing design doc rather than my guess.

The design doc (`PLAN_user_login_acl.md`) confirms the intent: **"beneficiary: View own account only."** So the dashboard over-exposure and unscoped funds index are deviations from the intended design — genuine bugs, not by-design. That gives me a solid target for what a beneficiary *should* see.

## Direct answers to your two questions

**1. Are all users corrected?** No — only `user1` (account 7). **11 more users across 14 accounts** are in the identical broken state (own an account, no role on its fund) — all on fund 2 (`user2..user8`, `user164..169`).

**2. Migration for prod?** Yes — I wrote `database/migrations/2026_05_24_000001_backfill_account_owner_beneficiary_roles.php`. It's idempotent and prod-safe: ensures the beneficiary permissions exist, then grants the fund-scoped `beneficiary` role to every account-owner who has no role on that fund — **never** downgrades an admin/manager, skips system-admins, runs at deploy via `php artisan migrate`. Reverse is a deliberate no-op.

## The catch — these are coupled

Running that backfill on the **current** code would hand all 11 users the same problems you just found: the coarse dashboard (admin-tier links) and the `/funds` leak. So the backfill must ship **together** with the lockdown fixes. Current state:

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| `user1` granted beneficiary (dev DB, live at :3001) | ✅ done |
| Funds index scoping (repo override + `withAuthorization()`) | ✅ done *in worktree* |
| Backfill migration (all 11 users) | ✅ written, **not run** |
| Dashboard role-tiering (beneficiary ≠ fund-admin links) | ❌ todo |
| Other unscoped indexes (Goals, MatchingRules, TradePortfolios, AccountGoals, PortfolioAssets, CashDeposits, Assets…) | ❌ todo — audit |
| `?as=` auto-redirect middleware | ⏸ approved, queued |

**Also critical:** `:3001` serves the **main checkout**, not this worktree — so none of my *code* fixes are visible there yet (only the DB role change is). To actually see/verify them I'd lease a preview slot that mounts this worktree.

Given the size and prod impact, let me confirm how far to take this in one go.
